verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents creating GPU machines from the console, API, or CLI, with an OpenAPI-backed REST API. An "ML in a Box" template comes preinstalled with ML frameworks and CUDA drivers, and SSH gives root access, so the core story is covered. One hands-on report describes SSH access as an uphill battle, and high-end GPUs such as the H100 require approval before use. missing for 10: independent corroboration of the 'within minutes' provisioning-to-running time, evidence that top-tier GPUs are available on demand without approval, and smooth hands-on access reports.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Machines are Linux and Windows virtual machines with persistent storage, GPU options, and free unlimited bandwidth.
Choose "ML in a Box" template that comes preinstalled with all the major ML frameworks and CUDA® drivers.
Bring your SSH key and connect directly to your VM with full root access.
Go from signup to training a model in seconds
